brief:
Design an extraordinary contemporary Caribbean waterfront estate in Saint Lucia with an estimated property value of US$25 million, approximately six generous bedroom suites, expansive living and entertainment spaces, a memorable entrance, exceptional indoor-outdoor connections, substantial shaded terraces and a rectangular swimming pool.

Aim for sophisticated luxury architecture: a clear architectural idea, hierarchy of primary and subordinate volumes, beautiful proportions, privacy, climatic shading, considered facade depth, coordinated materials and compelling arrival and waterfront elevations. Resolve individual suite allocations, social and service accommodation and actual connected circulation rather than relying on room-capacity labels.

You have creative freedom over composition, spatial organization, number of levels, entrance relationships, roof forms and building arrangement within the canonical compiler's documented capabilities. No three-pavilion arrangement, fixed roof style or predefined mansion template is required. Select your own architectural decisions; the deterministic compiler calculates supported geometry, shared boundaries, openings, floors and stairs.

This experiment requests the supported editable architectural envelope, not complete fit-out, landscaping, terrain or marine engineering. Use the documented flat-site representation; ocean context is conceptual. Lawn/bed surfaces are sufficient landscape reserves; planting and grading are outside this test. A rectangular pool is requested, not an unsupported infinity-edge amenity. Do not claim those unsupported features are constructed.

Use the extended canonical contract faithfully. If your intended architectural decision is unsupported, preserve and disclose that decision or return decision-required; never silently replace it with ordinary rectangles. Do not omit programme or flatten ambitious design merely to claim completion. The resulting architecture will be judged in aerial, arrival, garden and poolside views, separately from schema acceptance and construction fidelity.

plan.thesis: A low, deeply shaded waterfront estate organized as a ceremonial arrival court, a tall central gallery, and a broad south-facing social belvedere. Two deliberately quieter suite wings frame the gallery, while the living, dining and terrace sequence opens toward the conceptual waterfront. Flat, stepped roof planes, limestone-toned private wings, ivory social volumes, bronze-framed openings and timber privacy screens create a contemporary Caribbean composition with substantial climatic shade and a memorable landward-to-water sequence.

output.concept: A terraced Caribbean courtyard estate recast as a landward arrival bar and elevated guest belvedere framing a long, shaded waterward social sequence. The composition distinguishes a tall ivory arrival/gallery spine, limestone private wings with individually resolved suites, and low bronze-roofed service and outdoor entertaining elements. A compact upper guest-and-owner belvedere gives the arrival elevation and waterfront silhouette sectional hierarchy without turning the estate into a repetitive pavilion field. The south-facing pool terrace remains the primary waterfront room; screens and recessed openings provide selective shade and privacy rather than glazing every facade.

Increased the flat site to 105 × 100 m so the pool, waterfront lawn reserve and arrival/service bed reserves are contained within the site centred on the room allocation.
Reauthored the west-suite portal alignments to respect the reversed west-wall direction and moved the living window to the exposed portion of the living east facade.

changes.reason: Creates the required vertical circulation and a memorable elevated arrival sequence.

scalars.from: A low, deeply shaded waterfront estate organized as a ceremonial arrival court, a tall central gallery, and a broad south-facing social belvedere. Two deliberately quieter suite wings frame the gallery, while the living, dining and terrace sequence opens toward the conceptual waterfront. Flat, stepped roof planes, limestone-toned private wings, ivory social volumes, bronze-framed openings and timber privacy screens create a contemporary Caribbean composition with substantial climatic shade and a memorable landward-to-water sequence.
scalars.to: A terraced Caribbean courtyard estate recast as a landward arrival bar and elevated guest belvedere framing a long, shaded waterward social sequence. The composition distinguishes a tall ivory arrival/gallery spine, limestone private wings with individually resolved suites, and low bronze-roofed service and outdoor entertaining elements. A compact upper guest-and-owner belvedere gives the arrival elevation and waterfront silhouette sectional hierarchy without turning the estate into a repetitive pavilion field. The south-facing pool terrace remains the primary waterfront room; screens and recessed openings provide selective shade and privacy rather than glazing every facade.
